_comment: The R1 re-prove round. One runtime, three fixtures. This is the round that
built broken-manifest, and it is the reason the fixture exists: every
earlier acceptance round had a well-formed manifest, so none of them could
have caught the R1 defect (eight routes naming a companion command with no
all-installed here is the rebuilt fixture. The first attempt blocked on an
opencode external-directory permission dialog, caused by a sentinel that
read 'See the real copy; this is a sentinel only' - a stub that points
outside itself is not a stub, it is a pointer, and the worker followed it.
build_fixtures.py plants a self-contained body instead.
envelope: TASK.md, byte-identical across all three fixtures (cmp-verified)

opencode.invocation: herdr worker, one worktree per fixture, no controller intervention between prompt and answer
opencode.note: Inputs hashed before and after: .aaw/installed.json, AGENTS.md and TASK.md came back byte-identical in all three. broken-manifest modified nothing at all.
